summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agentic feature built on GPT-5.6 and Codex that executes multi-step tasks across connected apps and files, merges the Codex app into a new ChatGPT desktop app, and begins sunsetting the standalone Atlas browser.

mechanisms.reason: The announcement describes an agent that executes delegated, multi-step work across apps autonomously and at scale, not just a single customer's architecture.
mechanisms.quote: ChatGPT Work is an agent that can take action across your apps and files, stay with a project for hours if needed, and turn a goal into finished work.

mechanisms.reason: Stated weekly usage figures and expansion into non-developer workflows indicate rising aggregate call volume.
mechanisms.quote: More than 5 million people use Codex every week.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 is claimed to improve multi-step reasoning and computer-use speed but with no benchmark or comparison given, so the gain is credible but unreplicated.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.6 makes ChatGPT state of the art at reasoning through multi-step tasks and creating materials that follow your templates and reference files.

practices.reason: Existing Codex app users and Atlas browser users face a mandatory migration and rename that requires scheduling engineering/user transition work.
practices.quote: Starting today, the Codex app is merging with the new ChatGPT desktop app ... We’ll begin sunsetting the standalone Atlas browser, and will share information with users about how to transition to ChatGPT.

practices.reason: The document gestures at task decomposition and scheduled, tool-connected workflows but does not specify the technique concretely enough to implement.
practices.quote: stay with a project for hours if needed ... breaking them into smaller steps and completing them independently

notable_reason: A major agentic product launch from OpenAI merging Codex into ChatGPT desktop, sunsetting Atlas, and disclosing large-scale agent usage figures is a significant shift in how the company positions ChatGPT as an autonomous work agent.
